Koniguldon tried to get the ant-goats off of him, but his powerful hands were too slow and clumsy. For the third time, he collapsed under their weight, although their jaws and claws were too weak too leave anything but the slightest scratches in his metallic flesh.

As he tried to get up again, his hand slipped in a combined puddle of crushed ant and goat guts. Realizing that one of them had been smashed when he fell, he got an idea.

Repeatedly, Koniguldon rose, let the ant-goats swarm him, and then let himself fall. Soon there were dozens of corpses glistening on the reddish black rock. When there were so few left they could no longer hold him down, he rushed back to camp. What he found horrifed him.

His followers were completely covered by an enormous clicking, baaing mound of ant-goats. Here and there a groping Holnareem limb could be seen, but just barely.

After his fear dissipated, he laughed a deep, fierce laugh that wouldn't stop. He nearly lost consciousness, he laughed so hard.

"Help us!" one of his followers whimpered from deep under the pile.

"Gladly," he said, having finally laughed his fill. First, he grabbed a stone barrel filled with oil standing near the edge of the camp, and hurled it on top of the mini mountain of squirming ant-goats and miserable Holnareem. Next, he grabbed a huge chunk of flint and cracked it against a steel rod, until he has a coil of spare rope ablaze. Soon, he had the very top of the hill of goat-ants smoking.

The (relatively) small creatures panicked when the smelled their own flesh cooking, and before long, the camp was free of the pests.

Covered in smoldering ant-goat guts, Jamus approached the leader. "That was unexpected."

"You have a gift for understatement," Koniguldon said as he peeled a charred layer from Jamus's back. "Any casualties?"

A moment later, he determined that all were unhurt (if shaken).

He was about to give new orders when a scout who had been sent on ahead returned to camp.

"Compose yourself," Koniguldon snapped. "You're trembling. You were the only one who wasn't in camp when we were attacked, but you look as though you've been through a war."

"No... sir," the scout rasped. "But war comes upon us from atop the mountain. Behold: I do not come alone!"

Koniguldon turned abruptly as he heard a terrible cry.

The thing that rambled down the slope into camp was much taller than any Holnareem. Tall, and bulky, with broken bones jutting out of it like spears protecting a phalanx. Its stench was terrible. Although the Holnareem did not possess a particularly acute sense of smell, the miasma surrounding the brute was strong enough to sicken the strongest of them. It stank of death, and every part of it was dead, but horribly alive.

Its face was a bone mask that was itself composed of skulls, and it stretched one of its many limbs toward Koniguldon, an arm that was made of many corpse arms banded together. It let loose a howl like a hurricane of disease, challenging the leader of the Holnareem.

Two guards tried to block it with polearms. It swept them with a skeletal tail, knocking them off the mountain.

Its eyes burned with dead green fire, and it laughed, its rotting sinews tightening as it readied for battle.
